title: Cliff Richard's debut single Move It is released, reaching #2 in the chart. It is credited with being one of the first authentic rock and roll songs produced outside the United States.
text: Sir Cliff Richard is a British singer and actor. He has total sales of over 21.5 million singles in the United Kingdom and, as of 2026, is the third-top-selling artist in UK singles chart history, behind the Beatles and Elvis Presley.

title: Subscriber Trunk Dialling (STD) is inaugurated by The Queen when she dials a call from Bristol to Edinburgh and speaks to Lord Provost.
text: Subscriber trunk dialling, also known as subscriber toll dialing, is a telephone numbering plan feature and telecommunications technology in the United Kingdom and various Commonwealth countries for the dialling of trunk calls by telephone subscribers without the assistance of switchboard operators. Switching systems to enable automatic dialling of long distance calls by subscribers were introduced in the United K…

title: Humphrey Searle – The Diary of a Madman
text: The Diary of a Madman is a one-act chamber opera by the composer Humphrey Searle, who also wrote the libretto based on the eponymous short story by Nikolai Gogol. The opera was premiered in 1958 in Berlin.

title: Richard Addinsell – A Tale of Two Cities, starring Dirk Bogarde and Dorothy Tutin.
text: Sir Dirk Bogarde was an English actor, novelist and screenwriter. Initially a matinée idol in films such as Doctor in the House (1954) for the Rank Organisation, he later acted in art house films, evolving from "heartthrob to icon of edginess".

title: John Addison – I Was Monty's Double.
text: John Mervyn Addison was a British composer best known for his film scores.

title: William Alwyn – A Night to Remember directed by Roy Ward Baker.
text: A Night to Remember is a 1958 British historical disaster film, directed by Roy Ward Baker. It is adapted from the 1955 book by Walter Lord, about the sinking of the RMS Titanic on 15 April 1912, after it struck an iceberg on her maiden voyage.

title: James Bernard – Dracula directed by Terence Fisher, starring Christopher Lee and Peter Cushing.
text: Sir Christopher Frank Carandini Lee was an English actor and singer. In a career spanning over 60 years, he became known as an actor with tremendous screen presence and a deep and commanding voice, who often portrayed villains in horror and franchise films.

title: Buxton Orr – Corridors of Blood, starring Boris Karloff and Christopher Lee.
text: William Henry Pratt, known professionally as Boris Karloff (), was an English actor. His portrayal of Frankenstein's monster in the horror film Frankenstein (1931), his 82nd film, established him as a horror icon, and he reprised the role for the sequels Bride of Frankenstein (1935) and Son of Frankenstein (1939).

title: Leonard Salzedo – The Revenge of Frankenstein directed by Terence Fisher, starring Peter Cushing.
text: Leonard Salzedo was an English composer and conductor of Spanish descent. He composed over 160 works, including 18 film scores, 17 ballets, ten string quartets and two symphonies.

title: Expresso Bongo, book by Wolf Mankowitz and Julian More, with music by David Heneker and Monty Norman
text: Expresso Bongo is a 1958 West End musical and a satire of the music industry. It was first produced on the stage at the Saville Theatre, London, on 23 April 1958.

title: Valmouth, by Sandy Wilson, based on the novel by Ronald Firbank
text: Arthur Annesley Ronald Firbank was an English novelist. His eight short novels, partly inspired by the London aesthetes of the 1890s, especially Oscar Wilde, consist largely of dialogue, with references to religion, social-climbing and sexuality.

title: The Duke Wore Jeans, starring Tommy Steele
text: Sir Thomas Hicks, known professionally as Tommy Steele, is an English entertainer, regarded as Britain's first teen idol and rock and roll star. After being discovered at the 2i's Coffee Bar in Soho, London, Steele recorded a string of hit singles including "Rock with the Caveman" (1956) and the chart-topper "Singing the Blues" (1957).

title: Truman Capote's novella Breakfast at Tiffany's is published in this month's Esquire magazine (having been rejected for July's Harper's Bazaar). It appears soon afterwards as the title story in a collection published by Random House in New…
text: Harper's Bazaar is an American monthly womens fashion magazine that covers fashion, beauty, shopping, celebrity, culture, and bridal. Under the control of Hearst since 1913, it was originally published by Harper & Brothers.

title: The first volume of Shelby Foote's military history The Civil War: A Narrative is published in the United States.
text: Shelby Dade Foote Jr. was an American writer and journalist.

title: Jack Kerouac writes and narrates the "beat" film, Pull My Daisy (released 1959).
text: Jean-Louis Lebris de Kérouac, known as Jack Kerouac, was an American novelist and poet who, alongside William S. Burroughs and Allen Ginsberg, was a pioneer of the Beat Generation. Of French-Canadian parentage, Kerouac was raised in a French-speaking home in Lowell, Massachusetts.

title: Ken Kesey is awarded a Woodrow Wilson National Fellowship to enrol in the creative writing program at Stanford University.
text: Kenneth Elton Kesey was an American novelist, essayist, and countercultural figure. He considered himself a link between the Beat Generation of the 1950s and the hippies of the 1960s.
